questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a compound?
choices: A substance made of only one type of atom
A substance made of two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio
A substance that can be separated into its components by physical means
A substance that is not made of elements
questions.solution: A compound is formed when two or more elements chemically bond in a fixed proportion, creating a new substance with distinct properties. This definition distinguishes compounds from elements, which consist of only one type of atom, and from mixtures, which can be separated by physical means. The other options incorrectly describe elements or mixtures instead of compounds.

questions.stem: If a student wants to determine if a substance is a pure substance, which of the following observations would be most useful?
choices: It has a uniform appearance
It can be separated into other substances by physical means
It has a distinct taste
It cannot be separated into other substances by any physical process
questions.solution: The observation that a substance cannot be separated into other substances by any physical process is the most useful in determining if it is a pure substance. Pure substances consist of only one type of matter and cannot be broken down into simpler substances through physical means. Other observations, like uniform appearance or taste, may vary and do not definitively indicate purity.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the properties of a compound compared to its constituent elements?
choices: They are the same as the elements
They are completely different from the elements
They are a mixture of the elements
They are not affected by the elements
questions.solution: A compound has properties that are not the same as the elements it is made from because the chemical bonds between the elements create new characteristics. The other options are incorrect because compounds are not just mixtures of elements, nor do they retain the same properties as the original elements, and their properties are indeed affected by the elements they contain.
